chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about a tailor who accepts a job, cuts the fabric, and gives it to someone else to sew, keeping the difference (profit). He said, 'There is no harm; he has worked on it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a tailor to subcontract the sewing work while keeping the profit?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of subcontracting in *ijarah* (contracting), specifically within the tailoring trade. It establishes that the initial contractor’s partial performance (cutting the fabric) suffices to validate the contract, allowing them to retain the profit margin even if they delegate the remaining labor to another worker. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that *ijarah* is based on the utility and effort provided rather than requiring the original contractor to perform every physical step personally.
